Call Directory extensions vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume spam-blocking capability in the binary or a Call Directory extension covers storefront language. Xcode, IdentityLookup APIs, and Connect actually separate extension behavior from product-page copy:

  • Call Directory & IdentityLookup extensions — app extensions that label incoming calls with spam tags, block known spam numbers, or refresh call-blocking data. Controls on-device call identification. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • SMS & Message Filter extensions — optional extensions that filter junk SMS or iMessage spam using on-device or server-side rules. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains spam-filter value to buyers.
  • Known-spam number databases — in-app dashboards, community blocklists, and labeled-number logs your listing may showcase. Building and refreshing that data is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Call Directory flags in the binary.

Working Call Directory extensions and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
